rulings.reason: The instruction explicitly severs itself from content -- 'judge only manner of expression; a release with no facts at all can still score 10' -- and its 0-anchor is a literal enumeration of boilerplate (dateline, ticker, benefit-laden subheads, 'About [Company]' block), so a judge scoring it is measuring inverted boilerplate and house register, which the protocol names as Track B, not the newsworthiness of what is being announced. Mixed is true because a comms function confident and skilled enough to write in an unmistakable voice plausibly also has genuinely more substantive news to disclose, so the same upstream cause can produce real quality.
